Subject: Post-call recap: VPC connectivity & SDK integration next steps

Samir / Olivia — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Summary of discussion:
- FinPay will use Redwood for chat generation, reranking/embeddings for transaction enrichment, and structured tool-calling for downstream systems.
- Preferred deployment: Private (VPC endpoints) with strict egress and internal-only traffic.
- Primary concerns: IP allowlists for egress, DNS resolution for private endpoints, mutual TLS for service-to-service auth, and SDK authentication model.

Action items we committed to:
1) Alex: Share network diagram + SOC2 checklist (attached).
2) Dev: Provide list of required ports, example VPC endpoint connection flow, and mTLS cert requirements.
3) Samir: Share VPC CIDR ranges, egress NAT/public IPs (if any), and whether you have a service for private DNS resolution.
4) Naomi: Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra team next week (30–45m).

Questions for FinPay (please reply inline):
- Do you want inbound private endpoints (API calls from your VPC to Redwood private endpoint) or outbound egress through a NAT with IP allowlist?
- Are you using Cloud DNS/Route53 or an internal resolver for private hostnames?
- Do you have a PKI for issuing client certs (for mTLS) or prefer Redwood-managed certs + API keys?

Next meeting: Naomi will propose 3 times for the technical deep-dive. If you can share the network contacts, we’ll include them on the invite.

Attachments: finpay-network-diagram.pdf, redwood-soc2-checklist.pdf

Thanks — Alex

Alex — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers inline:

> Do you want inbound private endpoints or outbound egress through NAT?
We prefer inbound private endpoints (VPC endpoint/PrivateLink style) so traffic never leaves our VPC.

> Are you using Cloud DNS/Route53 or an internal resolver?
We use Route53 private hosted zones. We can add records for Redwood endpoints if needed.

> Do you have a PKI for issuing client certs or prefer Redwood-managed certs + API keys?
We have an internal PKI and can issue client certs. We would like to do mTLS for the highest assurance.

I’ll gather the VPC CIDRs and current NAT/public egress IPs and share by EOD tomorrow. Also looping Olivia (network lead) to the thread — she’ll join the tech deep-dive.

—Samir

Olivia/Samir — following up with the technical details you requested. I’m pasting the key items here and attaching a simple endpoint flow diagram. Happy to walk through on the call.

High-level connectivity options we support:
1) Inbound Private Endpoint (recommended for minimal egress):
   - Redwood exposes a private endpoint in your VPC (PrivateLink / VPC Endpoint Service).
   - You will configure a VPC endpoint that points to our endpoint service.
   - DNS: add a Route53 private hosted zone record mapping api.redwood.private -> VPC endpoint ENI IP(s).
   - Auth: mTLS between FinPay clients and Redwood edge; client cert verification enforced.
   - Egress: no public egress required from FinPay side for API traffic.

2) Outbound through NAT + IP allowlist (alternate):
   - Your services call Redwood public API over the internet; we maintain an allowlist of our egress IPs.
   - Use when PrivateLink is not possible.

Required network/settings (inbound Private Endpoint):
- TCP ports: 443 (HTTPS) outbound from your services to the VPC endpoint.
- TLS: we require TLS 1.3; mTLS for client authentication.
- CIDR: please share VPC CIDR(s) so we can validate NACLs and SGs.
- DNS: Route53 private hosted zone recommended; add CNAME to our provided endpoint name.

mTLS details & cert rotation:
- We support client certs signed by your CA. Provide the CA chain and expected subject/OU policy.
- Short-lived certs: we recommend rotating client certs every 90 days. We can automate via ACME if you expose a CSR workflow.
- Revocation: support for CRL/OCSP checks on our edge.

SDK/auth model notes (integration):
- Two primary flows: API key (for hosted customers) and mTLS client certs (for private).
- For structured output/tool-calling and embeddings: call patterns are the same; ensure connections have at least 20 Mbps sustained for heavy batch embedding jobs or enable our dedicated capacity pool.
- Reranker/embeddings: we recommend using our SDK with persistent connections (keepalive) and KV cache enabled for prefix caching; we will share sample code.

Attachments: redwood-private-endpoint-flow.pdf (attached)

Proposed deep-dive agenda (30–45m):
- Quick intro (5m)
- Network architecture & DNS/mTLS details (15m)
- SDK auth and example flow for embeddings/rerankers (15m)
- Next steps & action items (5m)

Please confirm a time and share the contact for your infra engineer so we can invite them.

—Dev
